facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy
underwent a live-related renal transplant 6 months ago
presented with a 14-day history of low-grade fever, dry cough, and anorexia
without dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis, or weight loss
afebrile on admission
heart rate 88 beats/min, blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air
bilateral inspiratory crackles
HIV ELISA was negative
Chest radiograph revealed bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates
High-resolution CT of the chest showed bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities
BAL fluid was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain
Transbronchial lung biopsy from the left upper lobe showed alveoli filled with inflammatory debris
